How will US midterms impact Indian equities, bond yields, crude oil?
 Historically, US equities have performed strongly following midterm elections. The S&P 500 has gained an average of around 6 per cent over the subsequent 60 trading days, data shows.
 President Donald Trump dances at a campaign rally at Lubbock Memorial Civic Center, Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026, in Lubbock, Texas.(Photo: PTI)
 Puneet Wadhwa New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 02 2026 | 6:38 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 The outcome of the US midterm elections in November could influence the near-term trajectory of global equity markets, with historical trends pointing to strong returns after the vote, analysts said. Gains, however, could be capped as bond yields and crude oil prices are likely to remain elevated.
 Historical data, however, suggest that Indian markets have not consistently replicated the performance of US equities during the third year of a US presidential term.
 An analysis of Indian market returns since 1998 — when foreign investors were allowed greater access to the domestic market, which had previously been relatively insulated from global developments — shows that Indian equities delivered an average return of 4 per cent over six months and 26 per cent over 12 months during the period examined. However, the performance was less consistent, with negative returns recorded on two occasions. ALSO READ: What Asian stock investors need to watch ahead of US midterm elections 
 The findings suggest that while a favourable global backdrop could support domestic equities, India's market performance will also depend on earnings growth, valuations and foreign capital flows.

 Geopolitical implication 
 For India, the US midterms, according to analysts at Emkay Global, could have more significant geopolitical than direct market implications. Analysts at Emkay Global expect Democratic control of Congress to increase scrutiny of tariffs and immigration policies, although this may not materially ease existing trade and diplomatic frictions. 
 The brokerage in an October 30 note coauthored by Madhavi Arora and Harshal Patel also flagged the possibility of a renewed escalation in the Iran conflict after the midterms, which could weigh on India's balance of payments (BoP), the rupee and domestic equity markets through higher energy prices and increased external-sector pressures.
 Historically, US equities have performed strongly following midterm elections. The S&P 500 has gained an average of around 6 per cent over the subsequent 60 trading days, 12 per cent over 120 days and 17 per cent over 180 days, Emkay Global said. ALSO READ: An unpredictable President, a grim White House: Trump faces down Midterms 
 However, the brokerage cautioned against extrapolating these returns to the current cycle. “Equities have already captured a larger-than-usual share of the typical midterm rally, while elevated bond yields and oil prices leave markets more vulnerable to inflationary pressures and a potential slowdown in economic growth,” Arora and Patel wrote.
 A gridlock situation 
 Jyotivardhan Jaipuria, founder of Valentis Advisors, said a split verdict in Congress could prove more favourable for equities than a Democratic sweep, as political gridlock could encourage a more balanced policy framework.
 “The political gridlock keeps spending in check and is good for bonds,” Jaipuria said, but cautioned that rising bond yields globally pose the biggest risk to equity markets. ALSO READ: Trump admin face criticism over inflammatory posts ahead of midterms 
 For Indian markets, Jaipuria believes a recovery in corporate earnings and more reasonable valuations could provide support. But the sustainability of any rally will depend partly on global financial conditions, with rising bond yields and geopolitical risks remaining key threats to the outlook.

 Hitesh Rathi of Angel One has said that unless Nifty delivers a convincing breakout above the 23,150-23,200 band, caution remains warranted.
 Angel One: Breakout above 23,200 in Nifty may signal short-term trend shift
 Hitesh Rathi Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 02 2026 | 8:06 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. 
 Hitesh Rathi, technical analyst (equity & derivatives), Angel One 
 It was an encouraging week of trade for Nifty , with the index recovering nearly all the losses incurred during the preceding week. Despite a slightly lower start, prices rebounded swiftly as buyers were quick to capitalise on the relatively lower levels. The index subsequently extended its gains following a brief phase of sideways consolidation, eventually closing the week at 23053, up 2 per cent for the week.
 On a weekly basis, Nifty continues to remain range-bound, extending its sideways trajectory for the fifth consecutive week. The sharp rebound witnessed this week from the 22,500–22,400 band reinforces the presence of strong demand at lower levels and highlights the significance of the rising trendline on the weekly chart, which has repeatedly acted as a sacrosanct support.
 Furthermore, the considerable improvement in overall market breadth and sentiment has helped ease concerns among market participants. That said, stiff overhead resistance continues to make the path to higher levels challenging.

 Going forward, unless the index delivers a convincing breakout above the 23,150–23,200 band, caution remains warranted, with a conscious effort to avoid chasing upward momentum. A decisive breakout above this resistance band would mark the formation of the first higher high–higher low structure on the daily chart, signalling a potential shift in the short-term trend.
 A weekly close above this crucial zone would further confirm the breakout on the weekly timeframe.
 In terms of levels, immediate support for the index is now likely to be found at the 22,950-22,900 band, followed by a stronger cushion at the 22,800 level. On the flip side, the 23,100-23,160 band is an immediate hurdle, followed by a stronger resistance at the 23,400-23,450 band. 
 Market participants should avoid getting carried away by the recovery witnessed across the broader markets this week, despite the stronger rebound in the frontline indices. The trend across multiple timeframes for both Smallcap and Midcap indices continues to remain aligned to the downside. Consequently, any potential breakouts in these segments should be viewed with caution, treated with a degree of scepticism, and approached with strict risk management. 'Earnings growth concentrated in pockets calls for stock-specific bets'
 Ajay Khandelwal says valuations have moderated and earnings remain resilient, with manufacturing, pharma, healthcare and capital markets among his preferred sectors
 premium 
 Ajay Khandelwal, Head of Equities, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund
 Abhishek Kumar New Delhi 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 02 2026 | 7:05 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 The scope for another broad-based correction from current levels appears limited, although near-term volatility cannot be ruled out, says Ajay Khandelwal, head of equity at Motilal Oswal Asset Management Company (AMC). In an email interaction with Abhishek Kumar , Khandelwal says his current focus is on structural themes where earnings growth is strong and visible. Edited excerpts:
 With West Asia tensions showing no signs of abating and oil prices remaining elevated, have Indian equities factored in the risks, or is there more room for further correction? 
 Indian equities have undergone nearly two years of time and price correction, underperforming global peers. Geopolitical tensions, particularly the West Asia conflict, and elevated crude oil prices have further weighed on market sentiment over the past six months.
 A prolonged period of high crude oil prices could put pressure on corporate margins, particularly in oil-sensitive sectors. However, the impact of elevated prices and supply disruptions remained relatively limited in the first half of 2026-27 (FY27).
 Meanwhile, valuations have derated from their 2024 peaks and are now below their long-period averages, while earnings have remained resilient. Near-term volatility cannot be ruled out, but the scope for another broad-based correction from current levels appears limited, except for further adverse developments or a material deterioration in earnings.
 What are the key triggers to watch out for that could add to the pressure on Indian equities or change the market’s course from here? 
 Key triggers include geopolitical developments and crude oil prices, which could affect inflation, corporate margins and the currency. Global interest rates and foreign institutional investor flows will remain important for market liquidity, while a strong initial public offering pipeline could add to primary market supply.
 Globally, any reversal in the artificial intelligence (AI)-led investment theme could redirect capital towards emerging markets, including India. Domestically, the impact of El Niño on rural demand and the sustainability of the consumption recovery will be critical for earnings. The US midterm elections in November could also influence trade policy, bond yields, and global risk appetite.
 Amid these macroeconomic headwinds, which sectors offer relative comfort, and which ones are you cautious about? 
 Our focus is on structural themes where earnings growth is strong and visible. Manufacturing, including defence, is supported by capital expenditure, indigenisation and rising order books, while pharmaceutical and healthcare offer durable domestic and global growth opportunities.
 Capital markets and new-age technology, including AI-led business models, are benefiting from the financialisation of savings and digital adoption. Consumer discretionary and durables are supported by premiumisation and rising aspirations.
 We remain cautious on staples, rural-facing and commodity-linked sectors, with an emphasis on stock selection.
 Small and midcap (SMID) stocks have outperformed largecaps despite the uncertain environment. Is the trend sustainable? 
 SMIDs have outperformed largecaps, supported by stronger earnings growth. However, the sustainability of this trend will depend on how earnings growth evolves relative to market expectations and valuations.
 Valuations of SMID stocks have corrected from their 2024 peaks and are now closer to their long-period averages. However, smallcaps continue to trade at a premium to historical averages, partly supported by their strong earnings growth.
 Stock selection remains critical, as the earnings growth premium is concentrated in select sectors and companies.
 Where do valuations stand currently, and which market capitalisation (mcap) segment is in the sweet spot in terms of earnings growth potential and valuations?
 Amid the ongoing market correction, valuations across mcap segments have moderated from their respective peaks in 2024. Large, mid, and smallcap valuations have declined by 32 per cent, 36 per cent, and 10 per cent, respectively, from their peaks. The three segments are currently trading at price-to-earnings multiples of 17, 23.2, and 21.3, respectively.
 Large and midcap stocks are trading at discounts of 19 per cent and 6 per cent, respectively, to their long-period averages, while smallcaps continue to trade at a 15 per cent premium.
 Largecaps appear relatively attractive from a valuation perspective compared with SMID stocks. The valuation premium in the mid and smallcap segments reflects their comparatively stronger earnings growth profiles.
 The second-quarter (July-September/Q2) earnings season is underway. What is your assessment of the results announced so far, and has the West Asia conflict started to weigh on corporate performance? 
 The Q2FY27 results announced so far point to a broad-based recovery in corporate earnings after two years of largely stagnant growth. Growth has been healthy across revenue, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, and profit, with several companies reporting results ahead of expectations. This points to an improvement in the earnings environment after a prolonged period of consolidation.
 So far, the impact of the West Asia conflict on corporate performance has been limited and selective across sectors. Managements are monitoring raw material costs amid elevated crude oil prices, even as earnings momentum remains broad-based and demand trends have held up.  Gold and silver prices may extend their decline in the coming week as bearish momentum persists, with investors tracking geopolitical developments, the US midterm election outcome and key economic data for cues on the direction of precious metals, analysts said.
 Manufacturing and services PMI data from major economies, eurozone inflation figures, and US unemployment and nonfarm payrolls data later in the week will also be in focus, they added.
 "In the week ahead, all eyes will be on the US midterm election results on November 3, and President Donald Trump's actions after that," said Pranav Mer, Senior Vice President, EBG - Commodity & Currency Research, JM Financial Services Ltd.
 Any escalation involving the US, Israel and Iran could sharply push up crude oil prices, while risk assets such as equities and commodities may face extended selling and liquidation, he said.
 On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures for December delivery fell Rs 3,539, or 2.5 per cent, during the past week to close at Rs 1.38 lakh per 10 grams, while silver futures declined Rs 16,587, or 8.5 per cent, to Rs 1.79 lakh per kg.

docs.title: 6 Brokerage consensus stock picks: Why multiple analysts see 14%-66% upside
docs.text: Brokerage consensus stock picks: Brokerages see further upside in several stocks spanning power transmission, consumer goods, financial services, airports, automobiles and telecom, with multiple firms assigning Buy ratings to the same companies. Adani Energy Solutions, Hindustan Unilever, Max Financial Services, GMR Airports, Bajaj Auto and Jio-Platforms feature in the reports, with target prices pointing to different levels of potential gains. The reasons vary by company, from stronger operating performance and expanding business segments to earnings growth and improving demand. Top brokerage recommendations Adani Energy Solutions Jefferies Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Adani Energy Solutions with a target price of Rs 1,980, implying an upside of around 62% from the reference price used in its report. The brokerage’s valuation incorporates its earnings estimates for the company’s transmission and smart metering businesses. The report said quarterly EBITDA came in 19% above estimates, supported by the trading business. Jefferies raised its FY27 EBITDA estimate by 6%, while cutting its FY28 to FY30 estimates by 4% to 5% because of lower expected spending on transmission and smart meters. It continued to expect EBITDA to grow at more than 25% annually between FY26 and FY30. Elara Securities Elara Securities maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Adani Energy Solutions with a target price of Rs 1,747, indicating an upside of around 35%. According to the report, revenue increased 53% year on year to Rs 10,075 crore. Transmission revenue grew 52%, while smart-metering revenue rose 111%. EBITDA increased 35.5% to Rs 3,101 crore. The report also cited an order book of Rs 87,220 crore, more than 15 projects and the addition of two new transmission projects. Hindustan Unilever Jefferies Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Hindustan Unilever with a target price of Rs 2,350, implying an upside of around 29%. The brokerage’s report described the quarterly performance as a slight beat against expectations. Its valuation was based on 42 times estimated December 2028 earnings. The report also identified raw-material costs, competitive pressure and demand conditions as risks to its outlook. ALSO READFrom chip design to chemicals: 3 stocks riding India’s Rs 1.64 lakh crore semiconductor push Nomura Nomura maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Hindustan Unilever with a target price of Rs 2,100, indicating an upside of approximately 15.6%. The report said underlying sales grew 15% year on year, ahead of Nomura’s estimate of 11%. Gross margin fell 395 basis points to 47.6%, while operating margin stood at 22.4%. The brokerage discussed core volume growth, new product performance and input costs as factors relevant to the company’s earnings outlook. JM Financial JM Financial maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Hindustan Unilever with a target price of Rs 2,225, implying an upside of around 22.5%. The report put revenue at Rs 17,157 crore, up 15% year on year, and EBITDA at Rs 3,775 crore, an increase of 5.1%. Adjusted profit after tax stood at Rs 2,688 crore, up 6%. Gross margin declined to 48.6% from 52.1%, while EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 23.7%. Axis Securities Axis Securities upgraded Hindustan Unilever from Hold to ‘Buy’ and set a target price of Rs 2,120, indicating an upside of approximately 17%. Its report recorded revenue of Rs 17,157 crore, up 15.2% year on year and 5.4% sequentially. EBITDA stood at Rs 3,959 crore, up 4.9%, while adjusted profit after tax rose 5.8% to Rs 2,844 crore. The report also noted a 394-basis-point decline in gross margin to 46% and an EBITDA margin of 21.8%. The report said Axis Max Life’s value of new business (VNB) margin reached 27% in the September quarter, beating Nomura’s estimate by 130 basis points. The improvement was attributed to a favourable product mix, including 119% year-on-year growth in annuity business and 20% growth in group protection, along with a lower operating expense ratio and improved product-level profitability. Nomura raised its FY27 VNB margin estimate to 26% and projected 19% VNB growth for the year. It also noted that Axis Max Life aims to reduce its expense-of-management ratio from 25% to 16% to 17.5%, while identifying proposed distribution reforms as a key concern for the business. Jefferies Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Max Financial Services with a target price of Rs 2,050, implying an upside of around 66%. The report projected annualised premium equivalent growth of 15% between FY26 and FY29. It also cited the recruitment of 67,000 net agents over the previous two years and the potential contribution from improved agent productivity. Jefferies discussed the Axis Bank distribution channel, credit life business and a projected 130-basis-point improvement in VNB margin by FY29. It expected VNB to grow at a 17% rate over three years. GMR Airports Jefferies Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on GMR Airports with a target price of Rs 135, indicating an upside of approximately 51%. The report said revenue rose 11.6% year on year to Rs 4,095 crore in the September quarter, while EBITDA declined 2.2% to Rs 1,476 crore. Operating expenses increased 21.2%. For its valuation, Jefferies applied 10 times FY28 EBITDA to the aviation business and 35 times FY28 EBITDA to the non-aviation business. Airport tariff regulation, passenger traffic and capital expenditure were among the risks identified in the report. docs.title: CCI clears Devyani-Sapphire merger, Adani’s Rs 3,050 crore IntelliSmart deal
docs.text: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved five proposed transactions across the food services, renewable energy, power infrastructure, financial services and telecommunications sectors, including acquisitions involving Aditya Birla Renewables, Adani Energy Solutions, Prosus and Vodafone Group. The approvals cover a range of mergers and acquisitions involving major domestic and international companies, according to separate announcements issued by the competition regulator on Saturday. Devyani-Sapphire merger to create restaurant business with over 3,000 stores Among the key approvals is the proposed merger of Sapphire Foods India Limited with Devyani International Limited, which would bring two major operators of KFC and Pizza Hut outlets in India under a single corporate structure. "The Proposed Combination envisages merger of Sapphire Foods India Limited (Sapphire) with and into Devyani International Limited (Devyani) and certain related transactions," the CCI said. Announced earlier this year, the merger is expected to create a restaurant business operating more than 3,000 stores globally, with an annualised turnover of around Rs 8,000 crore. ALSO READNSDL Q2 profit rises 10.9% to Rs 122.5 crore; income climbs 34.8% Aditya Birla Renewables gets nod for Rs 17,200 crore Shell energy business deal In the renewable energy sector, the regulator approved Aditya Birla Renewables Limited's proposed acquisition of the entire share capital of Solenergi Power Private Limited from Shell Overseas Investment BV. "The proposed combination relates to acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of the Target by the Acquirer from Shell Overseas Investment B.V. (Seller)," the CCI said. The transaction, valued at approximately Rs 17,200 crore when announced in July, includes Shell's Sprng Energy renewable energy business in India. CCI clears Adani Energy Solutions' Rs 3,050 crore IntelliSmart acquisition The CCI also cleared Adani Energy Solutions Limited's proposed acquisition of IntelliSmart Infrastructure Private Limited for Rs 3,050 crore. IntelliSmart is being acquired from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL). "The Proposed Combination envisages the acquisition of 100% of the equity share capital of the Target by the Acquirer," the regulator said. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Adani Energy Solutions' presence in India's smart electricity metering sector. ALSO READIAF’s drone roadmap: Rs 225 crore pipeline, 300-unit hopes and the long road to real orders Prosus subsidiary gets approval to acquire stake in Navi In the financial services segment, the CCI approved the acquisition of a certain shareholding in Navi Limited by MIH Payments Holdings BV, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Prosus NV. Founded by Sachin Bansal, Navi offers financial services through a consumer-facing mobile application. French firm Vega gets nod to acquire 16.2% stake in Vodafone The fifth approval relates to French company Vega SAS's acquisition of a 16.2% stake in Vodafone Group PLC. Vodafone operates telecommunications businesses across Europe and Africa and has a presence in India through Vodafone Idea Limited.

docs.title: How the ‘ReArm Europe’ initiative helped India’s defence exports hit a record Rs 38,424 crore
docs.text: India has emerged as a growing global defense exporter in recent years — eyeing a target of ₹50,000 crore by 2029. Systems now reach more than 18 nations amid an increase of over 5,500% since FY14. The country has also emerged as the third-largest arms exporter to Europe due to the 're-arm' initiative. "Our exports have reached an all-time high of ₹38,424 crore (which is about €3.6 billion). India became the third-largest exporter of arms to Europe mainly because of the Rearm Europe initiative. As a result a lot of standard ammunition of different types, artillery shells, and large- and small-caliber ammunition started getting exported to the continent in significant numbers," Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh said last week. ALSO READRs 20 lakh crore approved in defence deals — but when will the money actually flow? He also flagged a Bloomberg report that said Indian arms makers have sent at least $872 million worth of ammunition to European countries since the Russian invasion of Ukraine four years ago. The figure represents a 1,600% increase from the $49.2 million in arms exported to Europe during the 4 years prior to the war. The publication cited data sourced by Trade Data Monitor from the Commerce Ministry to outline the explosive increase in Indian defense exports. Third-largest arms exporter to Europe The Indian government is targeting ₹3 lakh crore in annual defense production and ₹50,000 crore in exports by 2029. According to a recent PIB release, there has been 56x growth in defense imports from the ₹686 crore reported in FY14. The private sector contributed ₹17,353 crore, or 45.16%, in FY26 while defense public sector undertakings (DPSUs) contributed the remaining ₹2,071 crore, or 54.84%, of defense exports. The country saw its annual defense production surging to an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY26. The figure represented a 15.6% growth over the previous fiscal and a staggering 110% increase since FY21. Data shared by the government in August also indicates a corresponding surge in defense exports — reaching ₹38,424 crore in FY26. According to the defense secretary, the 'ReArm Europe' initiative has significantly boosted Indian arms exports to the continent. Singh added that India also planned to expand its participation in European defense procurement through joint ventures with European partners as well as encouraging foreign companies to manufacture in India. The India-EU Security and Defense Partnership was signed in January this year — moving ties into direct operational and industrial defense cooperation. The inaugural session of the India-EU Security and Defense Dialogue was held in March 2026 to manage joint military logistics and supply chain integrations. Both sides have also entered negotiations to share classified intelligence for sensitive hardware. Successful deals have also been struck at the bilateral level — a key example being ties between India and France that allow co-development of advanced military technology, joint defense manufacturing, and deep maritime security cooperation. ALSO READIndia eyes scale-up in missile production, defence exports According to the Bloomberg report, three quarters of the arm shipments sent by India have gone to nations within Eastern and Central Europe. The 13-country block has been a major arm supplier for Ukraine and saw demand surge after the Russian invasion. According to Trade Data Monitor, India is now the overall second-biggest supplier of arms, including shells, mortars, propellants, and explosives, to these countries — up from 28th four years ago. Why is Europe rushing to buy Indian arms? The ReArm Europe plan was presented by the European Commission in March last year and provides financial levers for member states to quickly and significantly increase defense investments and capabilities. It aims to mobilize over €800 billion in defense investments across the continent over five main financial pillars. A key component is a national escape clause that allows member states to increase their annual defense spending by up to 1.5% of GDP for a four-year period without triggering EU deficit penalties. The European Commission estimated in a 2025 briefing that this could translate to approximately €650 billion in additional defense expenditure across the region over the next four years. According to the official World Bank database, India saw overall global exports for arms and ammunition reach $816.80 million in 2025. Romania was listed as the top buyer with an export value of $157.62 million while Slovenia ranked third at $105.23 million. Official data also shows India steadily embedding itself into Western and global supply chains — with a sizable components and munitions pipeline opening up with France and Belgium. Decades of post-Cold War defense cuts meant these nations had held very lean stockpiles even before Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The continent also faces a severe bottleneck in replacing what has been sent — with a desperate race to scale up industrial manufacturing and exports. According to a recent Euro News report, the EU intends to accelerate the disbursement of its €90 billion support loan to Ukraine as the country faces a financial crunch amid Russia's all-out escalation and blockade in the Black Sea. The bloc will provide Kiev with €32 billion in military aid and €13 billion in budget support during 2027. The loan includes €45 billion in payments for 2026, with the credit initially meant to last until the end of next year. A

docs.title: From inland depots to global ports: 2 stocks chasing a bigger share of India’s trade
docs.text: India’s container opportunity is more than just making shipping boxes. The country is developing a connected ecosystem of container production, rail transport, ports and shipping. Indian Shipping Container Market is expected to reach $361.6 million in FY25 and is projected to grow to $881.5 million by FY34 at a CAGR of 10.4%. Meanwhile, the major ports handled 915.17 million tons of cargo in FY26, Indian Railways transported 1,670 million tons of freight and global container-port throughput exceeded an estimated 1 billion twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2025. For readers: Two companies that offer different entry points into this developing ecosystem are CONCOR and Adani Ports. #1 CONCOR: The Rail-Linked Logistics Network Connecting India's Factories With Its Ports Container Corporation of India (CONCOR) is a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Railways, primarily engaged in transporting containers by rail and providing integrated logistics services. Its business covers inland container depots (ICDs), container freight stations, multimodal logistics parks, warehousing, port connectivity and first-mile and last-mile transportation. This makes CONCOR an important link between India's manufacturing centres and maritime gateways. Unlike a conventional freight operator, it combines transportation infrastructure with container-handling assets, allowing it to participate in several stages of an export-import (EXIM) shipment. The Inland Network Is CONCOR's Biggest Competitive Asset CONCOR has 68 terminals, including logistics parks, more than 15 logistics parks and 422 wagons. Its network connects inland industrial centres such as Dadri, Ludhiana, Kanpur and Tughlakabad with important western and eastern ports, including Mundra, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now CONCOR's container procurement programme also connects it with India's domestic manufacturing ambitions. Under the Make in India initiative, the company had placed orders for 21,620 indigenously manufactured containers. The company currently has a fleet of 56,008 containers. The distinction between container procurement and container manufacturing is important. CONCOR purchases containers to support its logistics operations; it is not itself the principal manufacturer in this segment. Its returns therefore depend on how efficiently the additional equipment is deployed. Specialised Cargo Opens Another Route To Revenue CONCOR is also widening the range of goods that can be transported through its network. In its Q1 FY26, CONCOR introduced specialised tank containers for transporting bulk cement and customer-owned tank containers for bulk liquids. It also reported the movement of industrial chemicals in tank containers from Paradip Port to Dadri and Khatuwas. Customer-owned equipment can be particularly useful because CONCOR may provide transportation and network access without financing every specialised container itself. Another important development is rail connectivity for the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal at Varnama, linked to the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) through New Makarpura Yard. Two Wagon Orders Strengthen The Transportation Backbone In October, CONCOR placed an ₹87.15 crore order with Southern Railway for 12 rakes of BLSS wagons. A few days later, it placed another order worth ₹485.93 crore with Braithwaite & Co. Ltd. for 24 rakes of BLSS wagons with Brake Van Type BVCM. The delivery deadline for the latter order is 20 June 2028. More rakes can handle more transportation capacity. They can also help CONCOR run more routes, given sufficient cargo demand and railway access. Bharat Container Shipping Line Could Extend CONCOR's Reach To The Sea Another development concerning the integrated container-chain theme is the proposed Bharat Container Shipping Line (BCSL). The Shipping Corporation of India, CONCOR, Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority, V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority, Chennai Port Authority and Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited signed a Memorandum of Understanding in February 2026 to establish BCSL. The proposed initiative is to connect the major ports of India with the inland markets through development of a domestic container shipping ecosystem. It is intended to strengthen end-to-end logistics, improve freight-cost stability and reduce dependence on foreign shipping operators. Q1 FY27: The Revenue Engine Holds, But Growth Remains on Track Two CONCOR reported a largely stable consolidated revenue performance in Q1 FY27, with growth in EXIM logistics offset by a decline in domestic logistics. The results matter to the integrated container-chain investment theme because they show whether rising freight volumes are translating into higher revenue and profit. docs.title: 59.4% profit growth, 68% valuation discount: Meet Bajaj Finance’s smaller rival
docs.text: It’s rivalry that is well recognised on Dalal Street between two leading NBFCs, Bajaj Finance and smaller rival, Shriram Finance, to grab a larger share of high-margin loans for commercial vehicles, gold loans and tractor loans. However, the Shriram Finance stock fell 1.9% on Friday to Rs 825, and it is hovering above its 52-week low of Rs 727.75 that was reached on 31 October, 2025. Why Shriram Finance's Cautious 15-17% Growth Target Spooked Investors Investors were disappointed with the growth outlook of Shriram Finance shared in the post-earnings conference call. The senior management of Shriram Finance in the earnings conference for September 2026 results had highlighted that they expect loan growth of 15% - 17%, going forward. Also, the senior management highlighted they are “cautious”, given the weak monsoon this year coupled with no signs of ending of the Middle East crisis and its impact on the local economy. Investors are also worried that Shriram Finance’s growth outlook would lag considerably that of larger rival, Bajaj Finance, and they sold the stock. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now The AUM Expansion Race: Shriram vs. Bajaj Finance in Q2FY27 For perspective, Shriram Finance grew its standalone loan book by nearly 17% y-o-y in the second quarter of FY27, and 15.3% y-o-y in the June 2026 quarter. Bajaj Finance, in its results presentation, has highlighted financial sustainability metrics, broadly referring to its growth targets, on a consolidated basis, of AUM (assets under management) expanding by 23% to 25%. As a result, the Bajaj Finance stock was broadly flat at Rs 939.2 on Friday, and not too far from its 52-week high of Rs 1,177.6 that was reached on 3 August, 2026. Also, with the RBI raising policy rates in October 2026, investors will be closely watching if both the NBFCs can fully pass on the rise to borrowers, and protect their net interest margins (NIM). Defying the 'Slack' Quarter: How High-Margin Credit Drove Q2 Volume A key operational parameter, loan growth for both the NBFCs is closely tracked by investors. Shriram Finance highlighted its loan book grew by nearly 17% y-o-y to Rs 3.29 lakh crore in the quarter. Also, high margin commercial vehicle loans grew by 19.4% y-o-y to Rs 1.53 lakh crore and they accounted for 46.5% of its total loan book. In addition, other high margin loans like passenger vehicles grew 20.1% y-o-y to Rs 71,541.9 crore and gold loans grew 68.2% y-o-y to Rs 8,974.2 crore. Core operational performance in Q2FY27 (standalone basis) – Shriram Finance v/s Bajaj Finance NBFCGrowth in loans (% change y-o-y)Net interest income (% change y-o-y)Bajaj Finance26%24.9%Shriram Finance17%39.7%Source- Quarterly results and investor presentation Meanwhile, larger rival, Bajaj Finance highlighted that its standalone loan book (assets under management) grew 26% y-o-y to Rs 4.26 lakh crore in the quarter. It has also highlighted strong growth in higher margin loans - gold loans grew 105% y-o-y to Rs 24,195 crore, CV and tractor finance grew 89% y-o-y to Rs 5,044 crore, and rural consumer finance grew 63% y-o-y to Rs 14,392 crore in the quarter. The September 2026 quarter is typically a ‘slack’ season for credit, with the monsoon season across most parts of the country and broadly sluggish business activity. In addition, the monsoon has been deficient in several parts of the country, with Karnataka and Maharashtra declaring drought in several districts / talukas coupled with no signs of the Middle East conference coming to an end. The double-digit loan growth by both the NBFCs in the quarter under review is commendable. The core NBFC functions of lending / providing credit facilities are reflected in the respective standalone results of both NBFCS. The NII Advantage: Why Shriram's CV Portfolio Outpaced Bajaj's Margins Another key operational metric that is closely tracked by investors is net interest income (NII). Bajaj Finance has not given its NIM – it has highlighted a 24.9% y-o-y growth in its standalone NII to Rs 12,150 crore in the quarter. For Shriram Finance, its standalone NII grew a healthy 39.7 % y-o-y to Rs 8,415 crore in the quarter, and grew faster than its bigger rival. Shriram Finance has a large exposure to commercial vehicle loans, and they accounted for 46.5% of its total loans, and loans in this segment have much higher interest rates, given the risk profile of borrowers. In addition, it has a strong focus on higher margin gold loans, passenger vehicles and farm equipment. As a result, Shriram Finance was able to grow its NII faster than larger rival. Its NIM was 9.5% as compared to 8.19% a year earlier. Asset Quality Under Pressure: Offsetting Rising Q2 Impairments Bajaj Finance has highlighted its net NPA (stage 3 asset, net) ratio was 0.53% for the first half of FY27s as compared to 0.77% a year earlier. Also, its impairment on financial instruments rose moderately – Rs 2,130.5 crore in the September 2026 quarter as compared to Rs 2,036.77 crore. Strong loan growth in high-margin loans helped Bajaj Finance’s standalone net profit rise 30.3% y-o-y to Rs 5,536.1 crore in the quarter. For Shriram Finance, it’s net NPA ratio was 2.3% as compared to 2.49% a year earlier. However, its impairment on financial instruments was Rs 1,877.4 crore as compared to Rs 1,333.3 crore a year earlier. ALSO READRs 10,000 cr government push: 2 smallcaps that could get a fresh growth boost Nevertheless, strong loan growth and higher NIMs helped Shriram Finance’s standalone net profit rise 59.4% y-o-y to Rs 3,677 crore in the quarter. The 20% RoE Benchmark: Assessing Capital Efficiency Across Both NBFCs Shriram Finance has a standalone RoE of 16.4% according to Screener.in. Bajaj Finance in its results presentation has highlighted an annualised consolidated return on equity of 20.6%. Return on Equity – Shriram Finance v/s Bajaj Finance NBFCRet

docs.title: Meet the hidden smallcap with Rs 1,180 cr orders and a plan to triple revenue by FY30
docs.text: Welcome to the latest edition of Hidden Gems Weekly. In recent weeks, we examined a Rs 350 crore cable maker looking to double its revenues, another that spent 37 years making bead wire and building relationships with leading tyre makers and one that wants to move beyond meter boxes. This week, we look at a company that makes precision-engineered components for the automotive industry and is now looking to expand into newer sectors. With a growing order book, rising margins and plans to nearly double capacity, this week’s Hidden Gem is aiming for a much bigger business. According to the Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA), the country’s auto component industry recorded turnover of Rs 7.6 lakh crore in FY26, growing 12.7% over the previous year. The industry more than doubled in size over the five years to FY26, registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 17%. Exports grew 5% to US$24 billion, while imports rose 13% to US$25.4 billion. The widening gap points to an opportunity for Indian manufacturers to develop specialised components and reduce dependence on imports. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now For domestic manufacturers, the opportunity is not simply to supply more components to India’s growing automobile market. Global companies are also looking to diversify their supply chains, creating opportunities for Indian suppliers that can meet demanding requirements for quality and precision. But winning orders is only the beginning. Manufacturers must invest in machinery, raw materials and inventory before those orders translate into revenue, and revenue must eventually translate into cash. Poojaa Precision Engg. Share Price Chart Source: Screener.in This is where Poojaa Precision Engg. comes in. The company manufactures aluminium die-cast and precision-machined components for automotive and non-automotive industries. Its integrated manufacturing capabilities cover design, engineering, melting, casting, machining, assembly and testing, with a portfolio of more than 600 stock-keeping units (SKUs). It has also entered aerospace after receiving customer vendor approval, taking its ambitions beyond its traditional automotive business. The financial numbers make the growth story compelling. Revenue increased from Rs 130 crore in FY22 to Rs 293 crore in FY26, while the operating profit margin improved from 12% to 18%. In the first half of FY27, revenue grew 68% year on year to Rs 210 crore, with the operating margin at around 19%. Management is targeting 50% revenue growth in FY27, followed by annual growth of 30-35%, with an ambition to reach Rs 1,000 crore in annual revenue by FY30. Poojaa Precision is positioning itself to benefit from this expanding market. Its growing order book, improving operating margins and plans to nearly double manufacturing capacity by FY28 provide the foundation for its next phase of growth. With revenue targeted to reach Rs 1,000 crore by FY30, the company is looking to build on its existing capabilities while expanding into new markets. Decoding the Rs 1,180 Crore Order Book The order book stood at Rs 1,180 crore at the time of its first-half FY27 earnings call. That is roughly four times its FY26 revenue, providing a substantial base of business to fulfil over the coming years. Management expects these orders to be fulfilled over approximately two years. An order book does not automatically translate into revenue or cash. Orders must be fulfilled, recognised as revenue and collected, with margins determining how much value ultimately reaches the company. Source: Company investor presentation Management has also indicated that annual requests for quotations exceed Rs 2,000 crore, with a conversion rate of around 8-10%. These opportunities could replenish the order book as existing orders are fulfilled. But requests for quotations represent potential business, not confirmed orders. The conversion rate will matter as much as the headline value of opportunities received. The revenue targets are ambitious. A 50% increase over FY26 revenue of Rs 293 crore would take annual revenue to around Rs 440 crore in FY27. Reaching Rs 1,000 crore by FY30 would require the business to more than triple from its FY26 level. The company has demonstrated an ability to grow, but investors must distinguish between the growth already achieved and the growth management expects to deliver. The important test is whether the order book converts into revenue at the required pace without weakening margins or absorbing too much additional capital. A large order book is useful because it provides visibility. Its real value, however, depends on the profits and cash flows generated when those orders are fulfilled. Growth Is Picking Up, Margins Are Holding Poojaa Precision’s operating margin increased from 10% in FY21 to 18% in FY25 and remained around 18% in FY26. It was approximately 19% in the first half of FY27. This suggests that the company has managed to expand its business while improving its operating profitability over the longer term. Higher production can help manufacturers spread fixed costs over a larger volume of output. But the benefit is not automatic. It depends on capacity utilisation, product mix and raw material costs. If capacity increases faster than demand, the company may have to bear the cost of additional machinery before the corresponding revenue arrives. Aluminium is a key input for the business. Changes in its price can affect margins, depending on the timing and terms of price adjustments with customers. Management has indicated that mechanisms exist to pass through aluminium price changes, although product mix and raw material costs can still influence reported margins. docs.title: Up to 208% profit growth, 135% returns: 2 auto stocks expanding for their next growth phase
docs.text: After GST rationalisation, India's automotive industry is growing faster than ever before. Rising vehicle demand, increasing premiumisation, and the transition towards electric mobility are changing the requirements of automobile manufacturers. This has prompted component suppliers to expand their product portfolios, increase value addition, and improve their presence in the automotive supply chain. The growth outlook remains encouraging. McKinsey estimates India's domestic auto component market to grow at an annual rate of 7-8% between FY25-30. The growth would outpace the broader automotive industry's projected growth of 5-6%. Rising demand for premium vehicles, higher component content per vehicle, and increasing exports are expected to support this expansion. The shift to electric mobility is creating another growth opportunity. India sold about 26.6 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) in FY26, up 30% from FY25. EVs accounted for 8.6% of total vehicle sales and are projected to cross 10% in FY27. This shift to EVs is also changing demand for individual automotive components. Automakers are focusing on lightweight materials to improve vehicle efficiency, performance, and driving range. One segment benefiting from this shift is automotive wheel manufacturing. Also, Indian car buyers are gradually moving towards aluminium alloy wheels, supported by rising premiumisation. Industry estimates suggest that more than 40% of passenger cars in India now use aluminium wheels. The outlook for future growth is also encouraging. The alloy wheel market is expected to grow about 12% annually over the next five years, compared with just 4% for conventional steel wheels. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now This shift in demand brings two leading auto ancillary companies with a significant presence in wheel manufacturing into focus. Both are already seeing the benefits of this changing market, reflected in their recent earnings. One company reported 208.3% profit growth in Q2FY27, while the other recorded an 87.5% increase. Their stock performance has also caught Dalal Street's attention. Both shares have delivered 135% returns so far in 2026. The question now is whether the shift toward alloy wheels can support their next phase of growth. #1 Steel Strips Wheels Steel Strips Wheels (SSWL) manufactures automotive components. The company designs, engineers, and produces wheel solutions and lightweight structural components for vehicles. SSWL’s manufacturing portfolio spans three major product categories: Steel Wheel Rims (52% of Q2FY27 revenue): This is the key product available for passenger vehicles, light and heavy commercial vehicles, tractors, two-wheelers, and off-road machinery. It features well-designed steel wheels that resemble alloy wheels while remaining affordable. Alloy Wheel Rims (45% of Q2FY27 revenue): High-margin aluminium alloy wheels designed for passenger cars, premium vehicle variants, and electric vehicles (EVs). Aluminium Knuckles & Structural Parts (3%): Lightweight vehicle components, such as aluminium steering knuckles and hot-stamped structural body parts. They help reduce a vehicle's unsprung weight, improve fuel efficiency, and extend the driving range of EVs. SSWL’s business model is strengthened by equity and technical partnerships with global steel majors. Tata Steel holds a 6.9% stake in SSWL. The company gets priority in the raw material supply chain and collaborates on new steel grades. Nippon Steel Corporation (Japan) holds a 5.4% strategic stake. The company is a direct Tier-1 supplier to Original Equipment Manufacturers globally. SSWL exports to 20+ countries across Europe, America, Asia, and Australia. It maintains long-standing OEM supply relationships with major car and tractor manufacturers, as well as prominent European heavy commercial vehicle companies such as Daimler, MAN, and Scania. Portfolio Shift: Alloy Wheels Drive High-Margin Realisations SSWL’s revenue mix is ​​shifting toward higher-margin alloy and lightweight aluminium products. In Q2FY27, alloy wheels accounted for 45% of revenue, up from 37% in Q2FY26. Sales volume grew by 33% year-on-year to 12 lakh units. Strong customer demand from non-Maruti OEMs supported this growth. SSWL’s market share among these OEMs exceeds 64%. In comparison, steel wheels' revenue share in Q2FY27 stood at 52%, down from 61% in Q2FY26. Strong demand recovery in Commercial Vehicles (truck wheels), tractor market share expansion from 43% to 45%, and surging adoption of styled high-end steel wheels drove this segment's growth. Aluminium Knuckles & Structural Parts contributed 3% to revenue. Export revenue surged 69% year-on-year to ₹187 crore, contributing 9.7% to Q2FY27 revenue. SSWL expects export revenue to cross ₹600 crore in FY27 and targets ₹1,500 crore over the next 3 years. This would be supported by export qualifications with major European commercial vehicle makers like Daimler, MAN and Scania. Capex Blueprint: 66-Lakh Unit Target and Greenfield Expansion The company can produce 210 lakh steel wheels, with 85% of this capacity currently being utilised. Alloy wheels capacity is 50 lakh units, with 89% capacity utilisation. The company has increased alloy wheels capacity to 54 lakh units. Work is underway to add 12 lakh units of alloy wheels capacity. This will extend the capacity to 66 lakh units. Commercial production is scheduled to begin in early April 2027. Moreover, it is also setting up a greenfield manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra. It is adding 25 lakh units of alloy wheel capacity. SSWL is adding 28 lakh units of steel wheels to target untapped markets and meet export demand. docs.title: The charm of a destination wedding
docs.text: The Indian wedding is getting smaller in one respect and bigger in another. Guest lists are becoming more selective, but couples are spending more on the people they invite, on accommodation, food, entertainment and experiences spread over several days. That is changing the economics of the wedding. A destination celebration is increasingly a multi-day tourism business, generating revenue for hotels, transport operators, restaurants, entertainers and local service providers. According to WedMeGood, over 60% of Indian weddings with budgets above Rs 1 crore are now destination weddings, while 89% of destination weddings take place within India. The wedding-planning platform estimates that the average wedding budget rose from Rs 36.5 lakh in 2024 to Rs 39.5 lakh in 2025-26. “Destination weddings have moved from a luxury niche to a more mainstream format,” says Mehak Sagar, co-founder of WedMeGood. “The biggest shift is from spending purely on visual grandeur to spending on the overall experience,” Sagar says. Couples are investing in better rooms, welcome events, entertainment, pre-wedding trips, honeymoons and personalised details, rather than simply expanding the guest list. “F&B, guest hospitality, entertainment and experiential elements are becoming part of the ‘wedding product’ rather than add-ons,” she adds. ALSO READGovt policy efforts helped lower poverty: Nirmala Sitharaman The broader economic stakes are considerable. KPMG’s 2026 report on the socio-economic impact of India’s events and experiences industry estimates wedding-linked household expenditure at around Rs 6.5 lakh crore in 2025. The figure includes spending on jewellery, apparel, catering, accommodation, travel, décor, entertainment and event management, rather than destination weddings alone. KPMG’s model of a representative organised wedding with about 350 attendees estimates visitor expenditure at Rs 1.07 crore and total direct economic impact at Rs 1.20 crore. Average spending by outstation attendees was Rs 52,771, against Rs 18,621 for local attendees. Rajiv Mehra, general secretary of the Federation of Associations in Indian Tourism and Hospitality (FAITH), describes weddings involving non-resident Indians as “a mini tourism festival”. Guests stay for several days, take local excursions and buy souvenirs, benefitting businesses beyond the wedding venue. “The wedding is no longer just a banquet booking. It can mean three or four days of accommodation, multiple F&B functions, local transportation, sightseeing, entertainment, shopping and curated experiences for guests,” he says. Beyond Rajasthan Rajasthan remains a leading destination, supported by its havelis and established hospitality infrastructure. Celebrity weddings have reinforced its appeal, Mehra says. Goa attracts couples with its beaches and resorts, while Kerala benefits from its wellness offering. Jim Corbett is popular with nature-seeking couples, and Kashmir is attracting interest at the luxury end. But the market is spreading. WedMeGood identifies Daman, Khajuraho and Mussoorie as emerging destinations. Radisson Hotel Group reports demand in Udaipur, Karjat, Lonavala and Mamallapuram, with Nashik, Chandigarh, Indore and Guwahati gaining interest. Government campaigns are also adding momentum. The Union tourism ministry launched ‘India Says I Do’ in 2023 to promote India as a global wedding destination. It subsequently partnered with FICCI on the ‘Wed in India’ expo in 2024 and the ‘Meet in India’ conclave in 2025. States are developing their own pitches. Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami said in July that the ‘Wed in Uttarakhand’ campaign would boost the local economy and employment. The state is developing Triyuginarayan, Omkareshwar, Ramnagar, Tehri and Mussoorie as wedding destinations. Dhami has argued that weddings can generate income for “local artisans, folk artistes, homestay operators, taxi drivers and many small businesses”, extending the benefits beyond hotels and resorts. Andhra Pradesh wants to develop Tirupati as a global wedding destination, linking celebrations with the town’s religious-tourism ecosystem. Special chief secretary (revenue) Mukesh Kumar Meena says the aim is to cater to different budgets. “A combination of premium, mid-range and budget-level venues and accommodation could enable families from different sections to organise weddings in Tirupati according to their requirements and affordability,” he adds. ALSO READLower rice output may stoke food inflation The state also wants guests to stay for two or three days and explore surrounding heritage, cultural and nature-based attractions. Meena cautions that this requires investment in accommodation, parking, public transport, connectivity and civic infrastructure, including water, power, sanitation and traffic management. West Bengal is also looking to work with private-sector players to develop wedding tourism. Tourism minister Shankar Ghosh said about 450 wedding planners had approached him with an interest in promoting the state. Goa, meanwhile, was named ‘best destination for resort weddings’ at the Wed In India 2025 Awards. Tourism minister Rohan Khaunte said the state’s combination of “luxury, culture, and natural beauty” continued to attract couples, adding that the government wanted weddings to contribute positively to the local economy and community. The competition is international too. Mehra identifies Thailand, the UAE, the Maldives, Italy and Spain among destinations competing for Indian weddings. Thailand, in particular, has an established ecosystem, with predictable costs, permissions and hospitality infrastructure. Yet he estimates that 80% of destination weddings involving Indians are held domestically. Food and culture remain important reasons to stay in India, he says. Retaining more business will require not just new hotels but a wider pool of skilled photographers, videographers, florists, logistics providers and tourist guides. Celebrating the location

docs.title: Doing more with less
docs.text: Big Tech is confronting an uncomfortable question amid its artificial intelligence (AI) boom: can companies become more productive with fewer people? As billions of dollars flow into data centres, chips and AI applications, technology companies are reassessing workforce sizes, hiring plans and the skills they need. Microsoft’s voluntary exit programme has brought this shift into focus, as AI redraws the boundaries between technology, productivity and jobs.The programme, described by executive vice-president and chief people officer Amy Coleman as a new approach to managing organisational change, offers eligible employees financial support and career-planning resources to leave the company. Around 60,000 employees globally are eligible, including those in India, the US, the UK and Canada. Microsoft has approximately 23,000 employees in India, though it has not disclosed how many qualify. Employees must decide by December 1.Coleman said the initiative gives employees considering opportunities outside Microsoft “a new choice to make that transition now with support”. The company has not explicitly linked the programme to AI replacing jobs. Its timing, however, raises a larger question: is AI making Big Tech smaller, or changing what a technology company looks like?The scale of workforce restructuring suggests the shift is already underway. Amazon eliminated 16,000 corporate jobs early this year, following 14,000 cuts in October 2025. Oracle has reportedly cut around 21,000 positions in 2026, while Meta announced plans to eliminate 8,000 jobs and leave thousands of vacancies unfilled. Cisco, too, has undertaken workforce reductions.Not every cut is driven by AI. Cost pressures, organisational complexity and changing business priorities are also at play. Yet as companies redirect billions towards AI, they face growing pressure to improve productivity, simplify management structures and generate returns on their investments.Jaspreet Bindra, founder and CEO of AI&Beyond and Tech Whisperer, sees a shift from headcount growth to “capability density” - getting more work done with smaller, more specialised teams. Routine coding, testing, reporting and coordination can increasingly be automated, allowing fewer employees to deliver comparable output.The difference in productivity between established technology giants and newer AI companies offers a glimpse of where the industry could be headed. “Anthropic makes $6 million+ per employee, Microsoft is a few hundred thousand dollars per employee. Big Tech companies are shrinking to work in a way similar to the new AI labs,” Bindra says. ALSO READApple doubles down on the desk, Anthropic files for an IPO, and the rest of tech goes ambient The comparison points to a different model of growth, in which revenue and output matter more than the number of people on the payroll. Microsoft, meanwhile, is investing approximately $170 billion in capital expenditure during calendar year 2026, with the vast majority directed towards AI infrastructure, data centres and advanced chips. “Headcount will no longer proxy for ambition; output per employee will increasingly define overall scale in the future,” Bindra says.For India, the implications could be particularly far-reaching. The IT services has traditionally relied on a pyramid-shaped workforce, with large numbers of fresh graduates handling coding, testing, maintenance and support under experienced professionals.AI threatens to narrow this base. If a smaller team using AI tools can complete work that once required several junior employees, demand for freshers could weaken even as companies seek more specialised talent.Sachin Grover, vice-president and head of GenAI initiatives at NIIT, says professionals will increasingly need to build, integrate, validate and govern AI-enabled solutions rather than simply execute predefined tasks. Problem-solving, critical thinking and the ability to use AI tools effectively will become essential alongside technical knowledge.India has significant advantages, accounting for 28% of the world's STEM workforce and 23% of global software engineering talent. But the size of its talent pool alone cannot guarantee employment if entry-level work changes faster than education and training can adapt.Manish Prasad, president and managing director of SAP Indian Subcontinent, says preparing Indian talent for the next wave of innovation requires sustained investment in how people learn and apply their skills. SAP aims to equip two million people in India with AI-ready skills by 2030, contributing to its global target of 12 million. Nearly 13% of its India target has already been reached through certification, student education and community programmes, the company said. ALSO READLessons from Binance hack: 7 steps crypto investors should take to protect their money Yet it would be misleading to interpret every layoff as evidence of AI eliminating jobs. Companies are also correcting earlier hiring excesses and responding to changing business conditions. Meanwhile, AI is creating opportunities in model development, chip design, data infrastructure, cybersecurity, governance and enterprise implementation. The question is whether these roles will grow fast enough to offset pressure on routine work, and whether displaced employees can acquire the skills needed to move into them.For Big Tech, the reset is about getting more out of fewer people as computing power takes on a growing share of the work. For India's IT industry, the challenge is more immediate: its traditional employment engine must adapt before the entry-level jobs it has long generated become harder to find.The AI boom may create enormous wealth and new categories of work. But unless those gains translate into broader employment opportunities, the industry risks building the future with fewer people while leaving a generation of aspiring technology workers wondering where they fit in.

docs.title: FPIs pull out of G-Secs for third straight month
docs.text: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) remained net sellers of Indian government securities for the third consecutive month in October, as elevated US treasury yields, geopolitical uncertainty and concerns over the rupee continued to dampen investor appetite. FPIs sold a net Rs 5,615 crore of government securities under the fully accessible route (FAR) during October, compared with net sales of Rs 10,602 crore in September, according to data from the Clearing Corporation of India. FPI holdings in government securities fell to Rs 3.56 lakh crore as of October 31, their lowest level in five months. Higher US Treasury yields have made dollar-denominated assets more attractive, prompting foreign investors to trim their exposure to emerging-market debt, including Indian bonds. ALSO READ6 Brokerage consensus stock picks: Why multiple analysts see 14%-66% upside “The continued FPI selling through the FAR route reflects concerns around elevated crude prices, rupee depreciation, rising US Treasury yields and uncertainty over India's interest-rate trajectory. Although the India-US 10-year yield differential has widened beyond 250 bps, this alone may not be sufficient to attract foreign investors,” said Kunal Sodhani, treasury head at Shinhan Bank. The US 10-year Treasury yield hovered around 5.25% for much of October, close to a two-decade high, before easing to 4.93% on Friday. India's benchmark 10-year government bond yield, meanwhile, closed at 7.41%, widening the yield differential between the two to 248 basis points from 195 bps at the beginning of the month. The Reserve Bank of India's recent rate hike and expectations of further tightening have also pushed domestic bond yields higher, exposing existing investors to mark-to-market losses. “The recent RBI rate hike and expectations of further tightening have pushed domestic bond yields higher, but investors are also facing mark-to-market losses on existing holdings. Additionally, currency depreciation and hedging costs can significantly erode the attractive yield differential,” Sodhani added. Market participants expect foreign selling to moderate if the rupee stabilises, crude oil prices ease, global bond yields soften and greater clarity emerges on the RBI's interest-rate trajectory. ALSO READUp to 208% profit growth, 135% returns: 2 auto stocks expanding for their next growth phase “Despite narrowing, the yield differential between US and Indian bonds remains insufficient to attract significant foreign inflows into debt markets. I remain cautious about debt inflows, as the rupee's recent stability may be short-lived given persistent underlying risks. Elevated crude oil prices also continue to weigh on the market,” said Madhavankutty G, chief economist at Canara Bank. Despite three consecutive months of selling, FPIs remain net buyers of government securities in FY27, with cumulative inflows of Rs 43,075 crore. These were driven largely by strong purchases in June and July following the government's tax concessions for overseas investors and the RBI's expansion of the FAR universe to include long-dated government bonds.

Published On Nov 2, 2026 | 08:02 IST 
 Last Updated On Nov 2, 2026 | 08:02 IST 
 AI Summary
 Global brokerages remain bullish on Dixon Technologies with target price upsides reaching nearly half its market value, driven by soaring revenue and expanding electronics manufacturing. However, margin contractions and the expiry of production incentives have sparked near-term earnings downgrades. How will component scale-up and upcoming joint ventures offset rising memory costs?

 Shares of Dixon Technologies will be in focus on Monday, November 2, after three global investment firms remained positive on the stock following its September-quarter results, with target prices indicating an upside of up to 45% from Friday’s closing price of ₹11,000.
Motilal Oswal reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating and raised its target price to ₹15,900 from ₹15,400, implying an upside of 44.5%. UBS maintained a ‘Buy’ rating with a target of ₹15,600, indicating an upside of 41.8%. Nuvama Institutional Equities upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’, with a December 2027 target price of ₹14,900, implying an upside of 35.5%.
Motilal Oswal raised its FY27 and FY28 estimates, while Nuvama cut its earnings per share (EPS) estimates for both years, citing lower mobile volumes and margins. UBS, meanwhile, expects the Vivo joint venture (JV) and component scale-up to drive earnings growth in FY28 and FY29. 
 Dixon reported a 48.7% year-on-year (YoY) decline in consolidated net profit to ₹343.7 crore for the September quarter, compared with ₹670 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 46.7% to ₹21,794 crore from ₹14,855 crore, beating the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of ₹20,235 crore.
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 6.4% to ₹597 crore, ahead of the poll estimate of ₹579 crore. However, EBITDA margin contracted 110 basis points to 2.7% from 3.8% a year ago, below the poll estimate of 2.9% and at a multi-quarter low. Gross margin also fell 200 basis points to 5.1% from 7.1%.
The decline in reported profit was largely due to a lower fair value gain on Dixon’s stake in Aditya Infotech. The company recognised a gain of ₹57 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹465 crore in the year-ago quarter. Q2 FY26 also included a ₹28 crore gain from the transfer of the lighting business.
On an adjusted basis, EBITDA rose 8% to ₹609 crore, with a margin of 2.8%. Adjusted net profit figures vary across the company and brokerage calculations and should be checked against the final results presentation before publication.
For the first half of FY27, revenue increased 35% to ₹37,341 crore, while EBITDA rose 2% to ₹1,060 crore. EBITDA margin declined to 2.9% from 3.8%. Operating cash flow was negative at ₹280 crore, while net debt stood at ₹73 crore at the end of the half-year, against a net cash position of ₹773 crore at the end of FY26. 
UBS described the quarter as directionally positive, with EBITDA rising 6% YoY despite headwinds. Its analysis suggests EBITDA per smartphone improved sequentially, helped by a better product mix and operating efficiencies. It also said two quarters of performance after the expiry of the mobile production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme reaffirm underlying profitability.
UBS highlighted the marginal increase in FY27 smartphone volume guidance to 33-34 million units from 32 million earlier. However, Q3 guidance of 7-7.5 million units implies only single-digit growth after four quarters of decline.
The brokerage flagged the delay in commissioning manufacturing at the Vivo JV, which has weighed on the stock, as well as higher working capital due to strategic inventory build-up. It expects the Vivo JV and component scale-up to support an EBITDA compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 35% in FY28-FY29, despite near-term memory-related headwinds.
 Motilal Oswal: Buy | Target price: ₹15,900 
Motilal Oswal said revenue and adjusted profit exceeded its estimates, while margins were broadly in line. It highlighted smartphone volumes of 9.7 million units in Q2 FY27, up 29% sequentially, despite a sharp decline in the broader Indian smartphone market.
The brokerage expects growth from new domestic customer additions, higher exports and the Vivo JV, which is expected to start contributing from Q4 FY27. It also sees further scale-up in IT hardware and telecom.
Motilal Oswal raised its FY27 and FY28 estimates by 7% and 2%, respectively, and expects revenue, EBITDA and profit after tax to grow at CAGRs of 29%, 36% and 39%, respectively, between FY26 and FY29.
Nuvama upgraded Dixon to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’ following the recent correction in the stock. It noted that mobile manufacturing revenue grew 39% YoY, with realisations up 50% even as volumes declined 8%. IT hardware revenue grew 42 times year-on-year and 60% sequentially.
EBITDA rose 6% YoY, beating Nuvama’s estimate by 3%. The brokerage, however, cut its FY27 and FY28 EPS estimates, citing lower mobile volumes and margins. It noted that Dixon maintained its FY27 mobile volume guidance of 33-34 million units, with Vivo consolidation expected from Q4 FY27. 
 The mobile and other electronics manufacturing services (EMS) division remained the largest contributor, accounting for 92% of revenue against 90% a year ago. Revenue rose 50% YoY to ₹20,093 crore, while its profit before interest and tax (PBIT) margin declined to 2.5% from 3.5%.
The segment included ₹2,160 crore in IT hardware revenue, ₹1,837 crore from telecom, ₹518 crore from Q-Tech and ₹171 crore from hearables and wearables.
Management attributed the margin pressure primarily to the expiry of mobile PLI 1.0 and elevated global memory prices. Memory, which earlier accounted for around 12-13% of a smartphone’s bill of materials, has become significantly more expensive. Selling prices have risen around 35-40% YoY, while volumes were marginally lower.

docs.title: Buy Indostar Capital Finance Ltd For Target Rs.240 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Growth phase begins; gradual improvement in profitability to follow 
 Legacy book run-down to drive credit cost improvement 
* Indostar Capital Finance (INDOSTAR)’s 2QFY27 PAT stood at INR132m (vs. INR115m in 1QFY27). NII grew 34% YoY to INR2b. Other income stood at INR407m during the quarter (PQ: INR367m).
* Opex rose ~10% YoY to INR1.3b, translating into a cost-to-income ratio of ~54.9% in 2QFY27 (PY: 63.6% and PQ: 58.2%). PPOP grew 58% YoY to INR1.1b. Credit costs stood at ~INR961m (PQ: ~INR815m). This translated to annualized credit costs of ~4.6% in 2QFY27 (PQ: 4% and PY: 3.1%).
* INDOSTAR is targeting ~35% disbursement growth over the next 3 years, driven by deeper market penetration, geographic expansion, and a strengthened distribution franchise, supported by a ~51% increase in the sales force, completion of product verticalization, and leadership onboarding. VF is expected to remain the key growth driver, complemented by the scaling up of MLAP, which is targeted to contribute ~10-15% of overall AUM (over the next 3 years), supporting gradual portfolio diversification. We expect INDOSTAR to deliver an AUM CAGR of ~26% over FY26-28E.
* INDOSTAR’s gradual run-down of the legacy portfolio and declining funding costs is expected to support lower credit costs and margin stability, driving a meaningful improvement in profitability. Management targets ~2% RoA by 2HFY28 and PAT of INR4.5-5b in FY29.
* We estimate a CAGR of 26%/42% in AUM/PAT over FY26-28 and an RoA/ RoE of ~2.1%/~7% in FY28E. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR240 (premised on 0.9x Sep’28E BVPS).
 Healthy disbursement momentum; Micro-LAP gaining traction 
* Total AUM grew 12% YoY and 2.6% QoQ to ~INR84.6b. VF AUM grew 13% YoY and 2.6% QoQ. Total disbursements grew 51% YoY and ~13% QoQ to ~INR14b. VF disbursements stood at ~INR13.2b, growing ~47% YoY and ~12% QoQ.
* Micro-LAP AUM grew ~177% YoY/ ~29% QoQ to INR2.8b. Disbursements in Micro-LAP grew ~174% YoY to INR740m. LTV in this segment stood at 40.3% as of Sep’26.
* INDOSTAR plans to launch its LAP business in Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh in 2HFY27, with a calibrated approach towards building the portfolio. It also intends to gradually increase ticket sizes, with the median ATS expected to stabilize at ~INR1m, even if this entails some moderation in yields. We expect the company to deliver an AUM CAGR of ~26% over FY26-28E.
 Key highlights from the management commentary 
* INDOSTAR does not intend to concentrate its portfolio in any single product segment and has consciously decided to restrict the share of any individual segment to ~35-40% of overall AUM.
* The company intends to pass on any increase in the cost of funds to borrowers, in line with the approach followed by other NBFCs.
* The company delivered a healthy 2QFY27 performance, driven by robust disbursement growth, improving asset quality and sequential NIM expansion. Going forward, the run-down of the legacy book and lower funding costs are expected to support credit cost normalization and margin stability, while a strengthened distribution franchise and improving customer profile provide a foundation for sustained growth and profitability improvement.
* We estimate a CAGR of 26%/42% in AUM/PAT over FY26-28 and an RoA/ RoE of ~2.1%/~7% in FY28E. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR240 (premised on 0.9x Sep’28E BVPS).

docs.title: Buy Indegene Ltd For Target Rs.718 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
All-around beat; FY27 expected to be better than FY26 
* Indegene reported a strong 2QFY27 revenue of INR11.2b (+39.5% YoY/ +5.6% QoQ; MOFSLe: INR10.9b), primarily driven by Enterprise Commercial Solutions, which contributed 71.3% to consolidated revenue.
* EBITDA stood at INR1.9b, with a margin of 16.5% (MOFSLe: INR1.7b/margin of 15.5% in), up 6.6% QoQ and 32.1% YoY.
* PAT stood at INR1.1b (MOFSLe: INR1.1b).
* We expect its revenue/EBIT/PAT to grow 30%/32%/35% YoY in FY27 in INR terms, along with mid-teen organic CC revenue growth and a gradual margin expansion. We value the stock at 25x FY28E EPS to arrive at our TP of INR718. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock
 Our view: Life Sciences and Pharma opex outsourcing key tailwinds 
* Management reiterated that FY27 organic revenue growth will exceed FY26 levels, with 2HFY27 expected to outperform 1HFY27, driven by large deal ramp-ups, improving client traction, outcome-based revenue recognition and AI-led productivity gains.
* Large client recovery: A client that slipped below the USD25m+ revenue cohort secured a USD5m+ deal, with management expecting recovery to the higher cohort within 2–3 quarters.
* AI-led growth opportunities: Agentic AOR reduced pharma content development timelines from months to days, driving pilot conversions and opening opportunities for larger enterprise-wide engagements.
* BioPharm-led synergies: Integration of BioPharm's proprietary data and omnichannel capabilities is strengthening cross-selling opportunities, competitive positioning and large-deal conversion.
* Revenue productivity improved, with trailing 12-month revenue per employee increasing to USD79.6k from ~USD69k YoY, supported by GenAIenabled delivery, workforce transformation and increasing adoption of output-based pricing.
* Deal momentum remained strong, with nine USD1m+ ACV wins, including one USD5m+ deal and two USD3–5m deals. Key wins included content platform migration, a global content factory mandate and global digital content management, with meaningful revenue contributions expected from 4QFY27.
* Cash and investments remained strong at INR13.9b, while net DSO increased marginally to 69 days from 67 QoQ.
1) Revenue ramp-up of the USD10m outcome-based omnichannel contract in 4QFY27
2) commercial scaling and adoption of Tectonic and Agentic AOR offerings
3) sustained growth across top-20 clients and customer diversification
4) achievement of a 19%+ EBITDA margin by 4QFY27
5) conversion of strong deal wins into revenue growth and operating leverage in 2HFY27.
We raise our earnings estimates considering the impact of new deals and the possibility of increased work outsourcing by global pharma and life sciences companies amid expanding drug pipelines, rising clinical trial activity, and increasing regulatory complexity in the life sciences industry. We expect Indegene to deliver a CAGR of 22%/31%/32% in revenue/EBIT/PAT over FY26-28. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR718 (based on 25x FY28E EPS).
