docs.title: Buy PNGadgil Jewellers Ltd For Target Rs.700 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Demand momentum intact; cost control drives margin beat 
* PN Gadgil Jewellers (PNG) reported consolidated revenue growth of 22% YoY to INR26.7b (in line) in 2QFY27. Retail revenue grew 31% YoY with 25.5% SSSG, while franchisee revenue increased 35%. Retail studded mix improved to 11.9% (vs. 9.0% in 2QFY26). The reported growth was partly impacted by the shift of Navratri sales to 3QFY27, which might have deferred ~INR2b of revenue, as per management estimates.
* PNG added two stores in 2Q, taking its network to 80 stores in 37 cities. It plans to add 23 stores in FY27 to reach 103 stores, with 8-10 openings in 3Q and the balance in 4Q, largely through the franchise route. From FY28, management plans 30-35 annual additions, with a 50:50 COCO/FOCO mix across legacy and light jewelry formats. Early traction in Uttar Pradesh is encouraging. PNG targets 30-35% revenue contribution from new geographies by FY30, from ~9% currently.
* Gross margin expanded 100bp YoY to 12.6% (vs. est. 12.2%), despite a higher franchise revenue mix (17% mix vs. 12% in 2QFY26). Adjusted for INR50m in inventory gains on unhedged gold, gross profit was broadly in line. EBITDA doubled YoY to INR2b (beat), with margin expanding 300bp YoY to 7.6% (beat), aided by a 21% YoY decline in other expenses. Management expects advertising and promotional spends to moderate in 2HFY27. FY27 revenue guidance of INR130b and PAT margin guidance of 4- 4.2% remain unchanged.
* PNG targets 30-35% of sales from new markets by FY30. While traction in Uttar Pradesh and an improving studded mix are encouraging, the ability of new markets to scale up sustainably remains a key monitorable. Consistent growth in new markets and sustainable profitability will be critical to validating the growth opportunity. We model revenue, EBITDA and APAT CAGRs of 19%, 24% and 17%, respectively, over FY26-29E. While positive on the long-term opportunity, we remain cautious on execution and the earnings trajectory. We reiterate BUY with a TP of INR700, based on 17x Sep’28E earnings.
 Key takeaways from the management commentary 
* Reported growth was understated because Navratri moved to 3Q this year from 2Q last year. Management estimates the 10-day season adds ~INR2b of revenue, which will now show up in 3Q.
* Management said Navratri demand was good, and soft gold prices are drawing buyers in. Diwali, especially the first half of November, and the wedding season look strong, based on bookings. Lower prices should support volume-led SSSG.
* Hedge coverage rose to ~80% from ~70% in 1Q, which reduces earnings sensitivity to gold price swings.
* The company ended 2Q with 80 stores and plans to open around 23 more stores during FY27, taking the network to ~103 stores by year-end. Most store openings are planned during 3Q and 4Q.
* From FY28, the company plans to add 30-35 stores a year with a 50:50 company-owned/franchise mix. About 17-18 of these would be legacy and the balance LiteStyle, each split equally between company-owned and franchise.
* We increase our EPS estimates by ~4% for FY27, considering a better operating performance, and largely maintain our FY28 earnings.
* PNG targets 30-35% of sales from new markets by FY30. While encouraging traction in Uttar Pradesh and an improving studded mix provide some confidence in the expansion opportunity, the ability of new markets to scale up sustainably remains to be established.
* Further, the strong EBITDA margin expansion in 2Q was aided by sharp cost cuts, thus the sustainability of cost efficiencies remains a key monitorable. We believe consistent execution across new markets and stable profitability will be critical to validating the growth opportunity.
* We model revenue, EBITDA and APAT CAGRs of 19%, 24% and 17%, respectively, over FY26-29E. While we remain positive on the long-term opportunity, we retain some caution on the execution and earnings trajectory. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR700, based on 17x Sep’28E earnings.

docs.title: Buy Intellect Design Arena Ltd For Target Rs.700 by Choice Institutional Equities
docs.text:
Growth Outlook Moderates; Long-term Platform Opportunity Intact 
INDA remains in an investment-led transition phase, with continued investments in R&D, AI capabilities and the expansion of its eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric platforms. While growth in license-linked revenues has moderated, newer offerings such as Purple Fabric and MSOCK are expected to gradually scale up. Although MSOCK could create incremental opportunities in enterprise modernisation and mainframe-to-cloud migration, the market remains dominated by traditional IT services players. We expect MSOCK to initially support implementation productivity and implementation-led revenues, with a gradual contribution to license-linked growth. We have revised our EBITDA estimates to factor in the evolving business mix and longer monetisation cycle, while valuing INDA at 16.0x average FY28E–FY29E EPS. Accordingly, we revise our TP to INR 700 and retain our ‘BUY’ rating, as we believe the long-term growth opportunity from AI-led offerings and platform expansion remains intact.
 Revenue and EBITDA Miss Estimate; License-linked Revenues Witness Slowdown 
* INDA reported Q2FY27 revenues at INR 8,467 Mn (vs CIE est. of INR 8,775 Mn), reflecting a growth of 11.7% YoY. The growth was driven by Implementation revenues which increased 16.3% YoY to 3,897 Mn while License-linked revenues increased by 8.0% YoY to 4,570 Mn.
* EBITDA came in at INR 1,677 Mn (vs CIE est. of INR 1,799 Mn), up 9.3% YoY due to higher SG&A expenses. EBITDA margin came in at 19.8% (vs CIE est at 20.5%), down 45 bps YoY and up 15 bps on a sequential basis.
* PAT for the full quarter came in at INR 1,041 Mn (vs CIE est. at INR 1,128 Mn), up 1.8% YoY due to higher investments.
 License-linked Revenue Growth Moderates; Deal Wins Steady 
Intellect reported Q2FY27 revenue growth of 11.7% YoY, primarily driven by 16.3% YoY increase in Implementation revenues, while License-linked revenues grew at a slower pace of 8.0% YoY. Overall deal momentum remained steady, with 21 new deals signed, including 8 Destiny deals. The deal pipeline grew 9.4% YoY to INR 131.2 Bn. The moderation in license-linked revenue growth was largely attributed to a 2.2% decline in Platform revenues, following the migration of a large credit union customer to an alternative platform after the Central 1 acquisition with possibility of further exits. Separately, INDA launched MSOCK to strengthen its AI-led enterprise modernisation capabilities, particularly in mainframe-to-cloud (M2C) migration. The company is also evaluating 3–4 acquisition opportunities, similar to Central 1, with the objective of using these platforms as an entry point to acquire customers faster and cross-sell its core banking offering.
 Margin Expected to Improve Gradually amid Ongoing Investments 
INDA continues to balance near-term profitability with strategic investments in AI, R&D and market expansion. MSOCK is expected to support operational efficiency by improving implementation and enabling faster project delivery. However, we believe INDA’s new products will take time to mature, scale up and generate a meaningful operating leverage. Accordingly, we expect EBITDA margin to improve gradually to 21.3% by FY28E, as productivity gains are likely to be offset by ongoing investments in product development and market expansion.

docs.title: Buy Shaily Engineering Ltd For Target Rs.4,074 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Healthcare drives growth; robust outlook intact Revenue/EBIDTA/PAT grew 24%/22%/20% YoY in 2QFY27 
* Shaily Engineering’s (SHEP) 2QFY27 result was driven again by its healthcare segment, while weakness persisted in the consumer segment.
* Healthcare revenue surged 78% YoY, driven by increasing traction in GLP-1 pen volume following patent expiry in India and Canada.
* Consumer revenue slid 14% YoY due to continued weak consumer sentiment in the US and Europe. Industrial revenue grew 23% YoY.
* EBITDA margin further expanded 81bp YoY to 30.4%, driven by greater revenue mix of higher-margin healthcare segment.
* Domestic revenue surged 33% YoY, driven by expanding GLP-1 pen volume supply to domestic pharma customers after opening of generic drug market.
* The company generated healthy OCF in 1HFY27.
 Key highlights from the management commentary 
* Healthcare: FY27 guidance of 36m pen is expected to surpass after ~20m pens already sold in 1H (1Q: 9m, 2Q: 10.4m). GLP-1 therapy should contribute ~70% of the total volume. SHEP has 100% share in Canada GLP1 markets and aims to replicate similar success in Turkey and Brazil, having the first mover’s advantage. Pricing pressure in pens is already built in in new contracts. Device for emergency use can come for commercial production by 2028 end, and it is working with two customers currently. 25m new pen capacity will start selling from Dec’26. It signed two new contracts for IP-led platforms for Semaglutide pens. It launched two-step reusable auto-injector pen, Shaily AI Toby, for GLP-1 therapy.
* Consumer: Business confirmation received for new product from an existing home furnishing customer; increased volumes for existing product from home furnishing customer; FY27 revenue likely to fall YoY.
* Consumer electronics: Started supplying in small batches; business confirmation from a new customer to supply five new products likely from 4QFY27; margins to be better than consumer and industrial segments.
* Semiconductor: Started supplying specialized trays from existing facility; revenue is likely to accrue from 4QFY27.
* UK subsidiary is expected to come back strongly in next few quarters.
We maintain our earnings estimates after healthy 2Q results. We expect a CAGR of 33%/44%/48% in revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY26-28, with a 32%+ EBITDA margin in FY28, driven by pen volume commitments from key healthcare customers. Robust RoE/RoCE (~29%/39% in FY28E) and OCF (FY26- 28: ~INR8b) will support the expansion of GLP-1 pen capacity by ~5x. Thus, we are constructive on SHEP and reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR4,074, based on 50x FY28E EPS. Slower-than-expected earnings growth could lead to a de-rating in the scrip’s valuation and pose a risk to our positive view.

docs.title: Buy Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd For Target Rs.2,300 by Choice Institutional Equities
docs.text:
Innovation-led Expansion Positions SUNP among Global Pharma Leaders 
SUNP continues to deliver a healthy growth and maintain its #1 position in the IPM. We project this momentum to sustain, supported by launches across its specialty and innovative portfolio. While the US business faces near-term challenges, we believe these should be offset by a healthy growth in India and emerging markets. Further, the addition of biosimilars from the Organon acquisition and a stronger position in the global innovative medicine market further strengthen our medium-term growth outlook. To reflect the projected weakness in the US, we lower our FY27E/FY28E estimate by 3.6%/1.1%, respectively. However, we believe SUNP is wellpositioned to leverage its market leadership and acquisitions to drive growth and synergies. We retain our target price of INR 2,300 and ‘BUY’ rating.
 Core Business Delivers; One-off Charges Weigh on Reported Earnings 
* Revenue grew 11.9% YoY / 5.9% QoQ to INR 1,61,987 Mn (vs. CIE estimate of INR 1,61,236 Mn).
* EBITDA grew 4.8% YoY / 7.4% QoQ to INR 47,439 Mn; margin contracted 198 bps YoY and expanded 41 bps QoQ to 29.3% (vs. CIE estimate of 29.3%).
* Reported PAT decreased 36.2% YoY / 31.3% QoQ to INR 19,885 Mn.
* The results were affected by exceptional items recorded of INR 12,688 Mn owing to anti-trust settlement charge and Organon acquisition-related cost. Adjusted PAT stood at INR 27,924 Mn.
 Innovative and Specialty Pipeline to Drive Next Phase of Growth 
SUNP delivered a healthy growth across markets except the US due to marketrelated and execution challenges in Ilumya. With the Organon acquisition progressing well, the management maintained its overall guidance of high singledigit growth. Excluding Organon, we project 11.7% revenue CAGR in the next three years, driven by:
 * India: SUNP maintained its leadership in Semaglutide and ranked #1 in the overall pharma market in India. We project the business to continue outperforming the IPM, supported by launches and volume gains. The company launched 15 products in Q2FY27.
 * US: The business continued to face pressure from Lenalidomide erosion and slower Ilumya growth, reflecting both, market-related factors and execution, challenges. While the rest of the innovative medicine portfolio performed well, the management expects Ilumya to normalise over the next 2–3 quarters.
 * EMs and RoW: Growth momentum is projected to sustain, supported by branded generics and a rising contribution from innovative medicines.
Despite near-term US challenges, we believe SUNP remains on track to sustain a healthy growth, supported by a strong launch pipeline, particularly in innovative medicine. We project EBITDA margin to remain at ~30%, despite higher R&D and acquisition-related cost

docs.title: Buy Greenply Industries Ltd For Target Rs.400 by Choice Institutional Equities
docs.text:
Resilient Demand Sustains Volume Growth, Profitability Improves 
MTLM delivered a healthy Q2FY27 performance, with double-digit revenue growth across Plywood and MDF, despite capacity constraint. Both segments reported an increase in profitability driving overall EBITDA higher by 57.2% YoY. Volume growth was limited due to capacity constraint, MTLM is incurring significant capex of INR 6.8 Bn to increase both, Plywood and MDF, capacities. Samet JV (on track for divestment 50% to 19% by January 2027) continued to incur a loss, reporting a PAT loss of INR 126 Mn, of which MTLM share stood at INR 63 Mn
 Q2FY27: Earnings Come in above Expectation 
* Plywood volume grew by 6.1% YoY to 23.0 Mn sq. mtr and realisation was up 9.1% YoY to 264/sq. mtr, driving plywood revenue growth by 15.5% and PAT up by 46.9%
* MDF volume grew by 16.1% YoY to 54,605 CBM and realisation remained flat (+1.9% YoY), which led to a revenue growth of 18.4%. Margin for MDF segment expanded by 690 bps driving EBITDA to INR 264 Mn
* Net revenue grew 16.1% YoY to INR 7.99 Bn (in line with CIE Est. of INR 8.1 Bn)
* EBITDA grew by 57.2% YoY to INR 892 Mn (beating CIE est. by 21.3%), with a margin of 11.2% (+291 bps YoY, +36 bps QoQ)
* PAT grew 166.4% YoY to INR 426 Mn (beating CIE est. by 21.0%); PAT margin was 5.3% (+301 bps YoY, +15 bps QoQ
 Capacity expansion to drive growth over the medium term: 
MTLM has planned a capacity expansion of 13.5 Mn sq. mtr at its Odisha plywood plant, entailing a capex of INR 1.3 Bn, along with an additional 15.0 Mn sq. mtr capacity at Sandila, involving an investment of INR 1.25 Bn. Further, the company is expanding its MDF capacity by 210K CBM at Vadodara, with a capex of INR 4.25 Bn. These expansions are expected to take the company's total capacity to 81.3 Mn sq. mtr in Plywood and 510K CBM in MDF by FY28E
We rationalise our capex estimate to account for elevated capex guidance and new plants for both segments. We believe persistent demand will lead to 9.7% and 19.4% volume CAGR for the Plywood and MDF segments, respectively. While we have increased our margin forecast by ~55–46 bps for FY27E / FY28E, higher depreciation and interest cost lead to a cut in net income. We now project Revenue / EBITDA / PAT to expand at 16.6% / 25.2% / 49.2% CAGR, respectively, over FY26–29E. We maintain the target price at INR 400/share by applying a PE of 22.0x. Our valuation implies a PEG of 0.4x. We, therefore, retain a ‘BUY’ rating with an upside of 42.9%.
Possible slowdown in real estate and home improvement activities and probable higher timber cost.

docs.title: Buy Welspun Living Ltd For Target Rs.260 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Double-digit growth across Home Textile and Flooring 
Welspun Living’s (WELSPUN) revenue grew 16% YoY, with HT and flooring delivering 15.8% and 19.3% YoY growth, respectively. Gross margin expanded 113bp YoY to 45.1%, while EBITDA margin settled at 11.9% (+563bp YoY), led by an improving business mix. We expect WELSPUN to continue delivering doubledigit revenue growth, fueled by volume recovery in the home textile segment, followed by a steady growing flooring business. Further, we expect EBITDA margin to expand to 13.2% by FY28, the business mix to improve in the home textile segment, and margins to stabilize at 2H levels in the flooring business.
 HT business up 16% YoY; robust growth in flooring 
WELSPUN’s revenue grew 16.3% YoY to INR28b in 2QFY27, with home textiles growing 15.8% YoY, while flooring business delivered a robust 19.3% YoY, driven by initiatives taken toward right-sizing the portfolio. For 1H, revenue grew 20% YoY, led by 21% growth in home textiles. Bath linen volumes rose 5% YoY, while in bed linen declined 4% YoY. Home textile exports grew 18.3% YoY, supported by improving demand across the US, UK, and EU, despite inflationary pressures in the US. Management expects US to grow in mid-to-high single-digits, while UK is expected to grow at ~20%, benefiting from FTA. US pillow business grew 2.4x YoY in 2Q, with both manufacturing facilities operational and reaching a combined utilization of ~67%. Both the plants at peak utilization are expected to generate USD80-100m by FY29. Management expects the flooring business to reach revenue potential of INR8-10b. Advanced materials remained under pressure, declining 7% YoY due to higher man-made fiber prices. Management expects the business to recover with normalizing costs.
 Continued EBITDA margin expansion in the flooring business 
In 2Q, gross margin expanded 113bp YoY to 45.1%, but cotton pricing continued to remain firm. EBITDA grew 120% YoY to INR3.3b, with EBITDA margin at 11.9% (+563bp YoY). The margin in the flooring business continue to improve, supported by the right-sizing of the portfolio. Management expects gross margin to remain at similar levels, hit by higher raw material prices, while guiding for a low-teen EBITDA margin. Cash conversion cycle improved sharply to ~44 days in 2QFY27 from ~82 days in FY26, supported by tighter working capital management, although partly attributable to certain business-related changes. Management expects a more sustainable cash conversion cycle of ~55–60 days
We expect WELSPUN’s core business, home textiles, to expand at a 16% CAGR over FY26-28 and drive a better margin mix. The flooring and advanced textile businesses are expected to grow at 17% and 9%, respectively, over FY26-28. We expect a CAGR of 16%/45%/104% in revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY26-28, led mainly by growth in the emerging business, followed by the home textile portfolio. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR260, valuing the stock at 15x FY28E EV/EBITDA. Key risks: customer and geographical concentrations, and commodity price movements

docs.title: Buy Motherson Wiring Ltd For Target Rs.45 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Earnings beat due to strong top-line performance Strong growth in FY27; margins to remain stable 
* Motherson Wiring’s (MSUMI) 2Q PAT at INR2.2b(+35%) beat our estimates due to a strong revenue growth and margin expansion. Copper prices rose 6% sequentially, but higher customer volumes and ramp up of greenfield projects supported a 160bp QoQ margin expansion to 9.2% (vs est. of 8%).
* On account of stronger-than-expected topline and margin performance in 2Q, we have raised our earnings estimates by 31%/17% for FY27/FY28. Optimal capacity utilization across greenfields and sustained demand momentum would likely keep margins stable. Overall, we estimate MSUMI to post a CAGR of 21% in revenue/EBITDA/PAT each over FY26-28. The company’s premium valuations at 29x/25.4x FY27E/FY28E EPS seem justified, given its strong competitive positioning, top-decile capital efficiency, and benefits of EVs and other mega trends in autos. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR45 (based on 32x FY28E EPS).
 Margins expand sequentially despite commodity pressures 
* 2QFY27 revenue grew ~47% YoY to INR41b (16% ahead of est.) vs PV industry growth of 25% YoY, aided by higher customer volumes, increasing content per vehicle, and participation in new model launches across both EV and ICE platforms. EV’s revenue share has now increased to 10% in 2Q.
* Copper inflation was steep, with prices rising ~6% QoQ (+54% YoY) and averaging INR1430/kg in 2Q.
* Despite lower gross margins, higher customer volumes and ramp up of greenfield projects supported 160bp QoQ margin expansion to 9.2% (vs est. of 8%). As a result, EBITDA grew ~34% YoY to INR3.7b, 33% higher than est.
* Due to higher working capital requirements, MSUMI turned from net cash in 1Q to having net debt of INR580m (ex-lease liabilities), leading to higher interest costs and lower other income.
* Due to strong top-line growth, PAT grew 35% YoY to INR2.2b (41% higher than est.).
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* EVs contributed 10% of revenue in 2QFY27 and 9.3% in 1HFY27, with the company participating in new model launches across both EV and ICE platforms.
* Management expects healthy industry growth to continue, supported by sustained demand, premiumization and new model launches. However, growth rates in 2HFY27 are expected to moderate YoY due to a higher base following last year's GST reduction.
* 3Q is seasonally a strong quarter due to festive demand, and management remains optimistic about sustaining the growth momentum, supported by improved capacity readiness and program ramp-ups.
* Copper prices increased ~54% YoY and 6% QoQ. Copper is largely a pass-through item, with recovery from most customers typically occurring with a three-month lag, although certain customers have a lag of up to six months. The company is negotiating with customers to recover higher copper and minimum wage costs, with management expecting improved financial performance within FY27 as these recoveries materialize.
* Management continues to focus on cost optimization, operational efficiencies, and maintaining a lean cost structure to improve operating leverage. It is also pursuing localization of imported components to improve cost competitiveness.
* The three greenfield plants at Kharkhoda, Gujarat, and Pune have ramped up well and reached optimal utilization levels, with their performance now being considered alongside the company's established manufacturing facilities.
* FY27 capex is expected to be approximately INR2b, broadly in line with the previous year. FY28 capex will depend on customer production schedules and capacity requirements, with the company yet to finalize the expansion programs and quantify the investment.
On account of stronger-than-expected topline and margin performance in 2Q, we have raised our earnings estimates by 31%/17% for FY27/FY28. Optimal capacity utilization across greenfields and sustained demand momentum would likely keep margins stable. Overall, we estimate MSUMI to post a CAGR of 21% in revenue/EBITDA/PAT each over FY26-28. The company’s premium valuations at 29x/25.4x FY27E/FY28E EPS seem justified, given its strong competitive positioning, top-decile capital efficiency, and benefits of EVs and other mega trends in autos. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR45 (based on 32x FY28E EPS).

docs.title: Buy MTAR Technologies Ltd For Target Rs.9,000 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Robust 2Q; momentum to continue in 2HFY27 
* MTAR Technologies (MTARTECH) delivered a healthy 2QFY27 performance, with revenue/EBITDA surging 2.9x/5.8x YoY, fueled by 2.4x YoY growth in fuel cells (57% of revenue), and 2.7x YoY growth in Aerospace & Defense (11% of revenue). The order book grew 4.6x YoY/16% QoQ to INR59.8b, with strong inflows (~INR12.4b).
* Driven by strong order book growth across segments, ongoing fuel-cell capacity expansion, robust nuclear opportunities, doubling of aerospace revenue in FY27E, and growing contribution from Product Solutions & Data Center Infrastructure, we believe MTARTECH is well-positioned to achieve growth across all segments.
* Factoring in strong 1HFY27 results, we raise our FY27/FY28 earnings estimates by 8%/9%. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR9,000 (55x FY28E EPS translating into a ~0.4x PEG ratio on FY26-28E EPS CAGR).
 Stellar topline growth coupled with better margins 
* MTARTECH’s consolidated revenue grew 2.9x YoY to INR4.1b (est. INR3.2b). EBITDA grew 5.8x YoY to INR992m (est. INR749m). EBITDA margin expanded 1,184bp YoY to 24.4% (est. 23%). Gross margin was 46.8% vs. 51.2% in 2QFY26 due to a change in the product mix. Employee costs/other expenses as a % of sales stood at 12.2%/10.2% Vs 24.6%/14.1% in 2QFY26, indicating operating leverage.
* Adj. PAT surged 14x YoY to INR598m (est. INR450m) for the quarter.
* Revenue from Clean Energy – Fuel Cell/Aerospace & Defense (A&D)/ Product & Others grew 2.4x/2.2x/7.7x YoY to INR2.3b/INR1.3m/INR438m, while Clean Energy – Civil Nuclear remained flat YoY at INR55m. Revenue mix between Civil/Fuel cells/Aerospace & Defense/Products & others stood at 1%/57%/11%/31% in 2QFY27 vs. 4%/72%/12%/12% in 2QFY26.
* In 1HFY27; revenue/PAT surged 2.6x/7.3x YoY to INR7.b/INR1.1b and EBITDA jumped by 4x YoY to INR1.8b, with the EBITDA margin expanding from 16% in 1HFY26 to 24% in 1HFY27.
* The order book as of Sep’26 stood at INR59.8b (vs. INR51.4b/INR12.9b as on Jun’26/Sep’26), with inflows of ~INR12.4b in 2QFY27 (cumulative INR41.6b inflows in 1HFY27). The order book mix stood at ~67.2%/13.5%/ 7.2%/12.1% for Clean Energy – Fuel Cell/Clean Energy – Nuclear/A&D/ Product & Others.
* NWC days declined to 50 as of Sep’26 from 172/60 as of Mar’26/Jun’26. The inventory/receivable/ payable days stood at 162/68/180 (vs. 145/82/ 167 in Mar’26)
* MTARTECH has a strong order book of ~INR59.8b as of Sep’26, driven by a healthy pipeline across clean energy (fuel cells), A&D, nuclear, and products & others sectors. The commercialization of new products and onboarding of new clients across segments are expected to drive further growth. Incrementally, enhancing wallet share with existing customers will also accelerate growth. MTARTECH is foraying into new high-growth sectors, which will contribute meaningfully over the coming years. We anticipate these initiatives to translate into strong growth and margin expansion.
* The company targets 3x asset turns on incremental capex (INR5b), with ~70% of the investment directed toward the fuel cell segment. The fuel cell phase-2 expansion is expected to be commissioned by Sep-Oct'26, followed by a multi-fold phase-3 expansion by Mar'27. The current order book is expected to be executed over the next three years.
* We estimate a CAGR of 85%/107%/127% in revenue/EBITDA/adj. PAT over FY26- FY28, and upgrade our EPS estimates by 8%/9% for FY27/FY28. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR9,000 (based on 55x FY28E EPS and translating into a ~0.4x PEG ratio on FY26-28E EPS CAGR).

docs.title: Buy Dixon Technologies Ltd For Target Rs.15,900 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Benefitting from healthy volumes and pricing improvement 
Dixon Technologies’ (Dixon) 2QFY27 revenue and PAT came in better than our estimates, while margin was largely in line. The company is continuously gaining market share in mobile segment, with strong mobile volumes of 9.7m for the quarter, up 29% QoQ, despite a 16% YoY decline in overall smartphone market volumes in India. Along with this, we have also seen a strong scale-up in IT hardware and Telecom segments, which benefited from product portfolio expansion and higher realization. Weakness was seen on non-mobile segments. We factor in better realization across segments, along with a slight delay in backward integration on displays. We expect FY28 to see full benefit of backward integration and improved volumes from Vivo-JV, exports and new client addition. We raise our FY27/FY28 estimates by 7%/2% to bake in 1HFY27 performance and slightly lower minority interest. We reiterate our BUY rating with a two-year forward DCF-based TP of INR15,900 (vs. INR15,400 earlier).
 Beat on revenue and PAT, while margin was in line with our estimate 
In 2QFY27, Dixon’s revenue and adj. PAT came in above our estimates, while EBITDA was broadly in line with our estimates. Consolidated revenue grew 47% YoY to INR218b (6% above our estimate). Beat on estimate was due to betterthan-expected execution across segments. Absolute EBITDA increased 6% YoY to INR6b, while margins contracted 110bp YoY to 2.7% vs. our estimate of 2.8%. Adj. PAT increased 19% YoY to INR3b (16% above our estimates). For 1HFY27, revenue/EBITDA/PAT grew 35%/2%/8% YoY, while margin contracted 100bp YoY to 2.8%. For 1HFY27, the company reported operating cash outflow of INR2.8b (vs. an inflow of INR8.8b last year), mainly due to higher NWC requirements, led by a surge in inventory and receivables.
 Smartphone volumes and realizations remained strong in 2QFY27 
Mobile and EMS segment revenue grew by 50% YoY, led by growth in smartphone and IT hardware/Telecom segment. Smartphone volumes stood at 9.7m during 2QFY27, and up 29% QoQ. The company has been gaining market share as smartphone industry volumes have declined 16% YoY over the same period. Dixon has maintained its full-year smartphone volume guidance of 33- 34m, excluding Vivo JV, for FY27. Volume ramp-up from Vivo JV is slower than our expectations, and we expect contribution to start happening from 4QFY27. For FY28, we expect Dixon to grow volumes through 1) new domestic client addition, which can add up 6-8m incremental volumes, 2) higher exports from anchor client Motorola and Transcion from 3.5m in FY27 to nearly 5-6m in FY28, and 3) 18-20m from Vivo volume addition. We bake in 37.3m/55m smartphone volumes for FY27/28, including Vivo JV volumes. IT hardware and telecom segments are benefitting from volume growth, product portfolio expansion and higher realization. We raise our revenue estimates for Mobile and EMS segments to bake in better-than-expected realization and expect ~93% contribution in overall revenue from this segment.
 IT hardware and Telecom ramp-up driven by volume, prices and product portfolio ramp-up 
IT hardware/telecom businesses are scaling up, with 2Q revenue of INR21.6b/ INR18.4b. IT hardware revenue is targeted at INR60-65b in FY27 and INR150-200b over the next couple of years, supported by increasing customer traction, portfolio expansion, and the 60:40 Inventec JV, which is expected to commence operations in 4QFY27. Laptop and tablet volumes are expected to reach 1.3-1.4m units in FY27 and 1.8-2m units in FY28, with a longer-term target of 4m units. While IT hardware margins currently stand at 2-2.3%, the company is targeting 25-30% BOM localization through backward integration into displays, SSDs and mechanical components, which could support 80-200bp of margin improvement over time. In telecom, Dixon is moving toward higher-complexity products, including microwave backhaul radios, optical platforms, industrial radios and network terminals, with exports of microwave radios expected to commence in FY27. GemTech JV, with initial capex of INR500-600m, is expected to begin commercial production in FY28, while discussions for aggregation routers and opportunities in IPTV set-top boxes provide further avenues for portfolio expansion.
 Other non-mobile segments witnessing weak demand 
Non-mobile segments such as consumer electronics, refrigerator, lighting are facing challenging times in terms of weak demand and inflationary pressure. Company is introducing new products in each category to improve volumes. Home appliances segment has seen a good volume growth and Dixon already has a 33% market share in this segment. We revise our estimates for these segments to factor in 1HFY27 performance.
 Backward integration initiatives to aid margin in future 
EBITDA margin declined 110bp YoY as benefit from PLI1.0 got over from Mar’26 along with higher inflationary pressure across RM and freight costs. Higher realization across segments also impacted demand for non-mobile segments. Mobile and EMS segment margins were down 100bp YoY, while consumer electronics margin was down 50bp YoY and home appliances margin was down 350bp mainly on higher cost of chips. Backward integration for display facility for mobile will commence trial production from 4QFY27 and mass production from FY28. Qtech camera module expansion plan is on track. We factor in delay in backward integration initiatives on display modules and expect margin to start recovering from FY28 onwards as these initiatives yield results. We expect EBITDA margin of 2.9%/3.6%/4.4% for FY27/28/29.
We raise our FY27/FY28 estimates by 7%/2% to bake in 1HFY27 performance and slightly lower minority interest. We, thus, expect a CAGR of 29%/36%/39% in revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY26-FY29, with EBITDA margin of 2.9% for FY27, which is expected to increase to 3.6%/4.4% over FY28/29 as backward integration initiatives start factoring in. The stock is currently trading at 73.
